title: Home Depot vs. Walmart: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Home Depot vs. Walmart: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Mike Schwenk, The Motley Fool
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 9:20 AM MST 8 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Deciding between Home Depot (NYSE:HD) and Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) comes down to weighing a possible pickup in housing-related spending against Walmart's steadier growth in everyday essentials.

While both companies serve as anchors for American consumers, they operate at opposite ends of the retail spectrum. Home Depot focuses on projects for homeowners and professionals, and Walmart sells a broad range of essentials and discretionary goods in 19 countries.

The case for Home Depot

Home Depot serves two customer groups, do-it-yourself (DIY) homeowners and professionals (Pros) such as remodelers and general contractors. The company operated 2,359 stores at the end of fiscal 2025, according to its annual report. It has also expanded into specialty distribution.

Home Depot acquired SRS, a specialty trade distribution company, in fiscal 2024, and SRS completed the acquisition of GMS, a distributor of drywall and other construction products, in fiscal 2025. Home Depot says SRS had more than 1,340 locations at the end of the second quarter of fiscal 2026.

In the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, revenue reached approximately $164.7 billion, a 3.2% increase from the prior fiscal year that included an extra week worth about $2.5 billion in sales.

Reported net income for the same period was nearly $14.2 billion, down about 4.4% from the roughly $14.8 billion earned in the previous year. Adjusted diluted earnings per share fell about 3.6% to $14.69 from $15.24, according to the company's release.

As of its Feb. 1, 2026, balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio reached nearly 5.1x, counting both borrowings and lease obligations against shareholder equity. That indicates the company uses significant leverage. By the end of the second quarter on Aug. 2, 2026, the same ratio had eased to about 3.8x as equity rose and total debt fell by nearly $3 billion.

The current ratio, a measure of assets available to cover short-term obligations, was approximately 1.1x at fiscal year-end. For fiscal 2025, the company generated nearly $12.6 billion in free cash flow, defined as operating cash flow minus capital expenditures.

In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, which ended Aug. 2, 2026, sales rose 5.7% to $47.9 billion and comparable sales rose 1.7%, according to the company's Aug. 18 earnings release.

Home Depot reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 guidance, which calls for total sales growth of approximately 2.5% to 4.5% and comparable sales growth of approximately flat to 2%. It expects diluted earnings per share to grow approximately flat to 4% from $14.23 in fiscal 2025.

title: Is COST a Buy as Strong Growth Meets a Premium Earnings Valuation?

Is COST a Buy as Strong Growth Meets a Premium Earnings Valuation?
Sumit Singh

COST
TGT
WMT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Costco Wholesale Corporation COST pairs durable membership economics with steady sales growth and expanding digital reach. Fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues reached $95.72 billion, while earnings came in at $6.60 per share, excluding a 15-cent nonrecurring benefit related to tariff refunds.

The growth case remains attractive, but the stock already reflects much of that quality. Investors must weigh Costco's operating consistency against a forward earnings multiple that sits well above its industry and the broader market.

Costco's Growth Engine Remains Strong

The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for fiscal 2027 revenues of $328.53 billion, up 8.4% from fiscal 2026. Earnings are projected to rise 11% to $22.70 per share, extending Costco's multiyear earnings compounding.

Fourth-quarter comparable sales increased 9.4%, or 6.7% after excluding gasoline-price and foreign-exchange effects. Shopping frequency rose 3.3%, supporting the view that growth is being driven by continued member engagement rather than price alone.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

COST's Membership Economics Add Durability

Paid memberships increased 3.8% to 84.1 million in fiscal 2026, while Executive memberships climbed 9.4% to 42.3 million. Executive members accounted for 75.2% of worldwide sales, giving Costco a large base of higher-spending customers.

Renewal rates reached 92.3% in the United States and Canada and 89.8% worldwide. Membership fee income also grew 7.3% in the fourth quarter, reinforcing the recurring-revenue foundation of the warehouse model.

Costco's Digital Gains Broaden the Opportunity

Digitally enabled sales exceeded $33 billion in fiscal 2026 and increased more than 20%. Fourth-quarter digitally enabled comparable sales rose 19.5%, while website and app traffic advanced 30% as Costco expanded delivery partnerships and personalization efforts.

The competitive benchmark remains demanding. Walmart Inc. WMT reported 23% global e-commerce growth in its fiscal 2027 second quarter, while Target Corporation TGT posted 8.7% digital comparable-sales growth in second-quarter fiscal 2026. Costco's digital momentum therefore adds another growth channel without replacing its warehouse-led model.

COST's Premium Valuation Raises the Hurdle

COST trades at 42.3X forward 12-month earnings, compared with 28.7X for the Zacks sub-industry and 19.6X for the S&P 500. The stock's five-year median multiple is 42.7X, indicating that investors have long assigned Costco a premium valuation.

That premium still reduces the margin for error. Slower earnings growth, softer comparable sales or a reassessment of premium retail valuations could pressure the shares even if the underlying business remains healthy.

title: What the Latest Fed Decision Means for Costco, Walmart, Target, and Home Depot
detail:
What the Latest Fed Decision Means for Costco, Walmart, Target, and Home Depot
Ben Gran, The Motley Fool
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 6:14 AM MST 7 min read
WMT
TGT
COST
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

When interest rates go up, that tends to be bad news for stocks. But not all stocks are affected the same way by rising rates. At their most recent meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Sept. 16, the central bankers hiked the benchmark federal funds rate by 0.25 percentage points. Inflation in September came in slightly hotter than expected, with a year-over-year CPI increase of 3.7%. That suggests that the Fed might hike rates again in 2026, as the FOMC will meet two more times this year, on Oct. 28 and Dec. 9.

When the Fed hikes interest rates, its goal is often to slow inflation -- and tap the brakes on economic growth. This can have negative effects on job growth, borrowing costs, and consumer spending. Some retail stocks might suffer more from a consumer spending slowdown than others. A few important retail stocks to watch right now are Costco (NASDAQ: COST), Home Depot (NYSE: HD), Target (NYSE: TGT), and Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Here's how these four retail stocks have performed since the federal funds rate hike on Sept. 16:

COST Total Return Level data by YCharts.

A 25-basis-point rate hike is unlikely to be a game changer for any stock. But some companies are more rate-sensitive than others. All four of these retailers have distinct strengths and vulnerabilities that would come into play in a rising interest-rate environment.

Let's look at which of these retail stocks are more likely to be winners if the Fed hikes interest rates again in 2026, and which might be losers.

Image source: Getty Images.
Costco: Affluent consumers unfazed by higher gas prices

Costco might be better positioned than most retailers to thrive in an environment of higher inflation and rising interest rates. That's because Costco's membership model creates a high level of customer loyalty, and the retailer tends to be popular with higher-income customers. According to a June YouGov survey, 11% of Americans in households with gross incomes of $150,000 or more do most of their food and other grocery shopping at Costco. These more affluent households are likely to be less bothered by high inflation.

A major factor in the Fed hiking interest rates is inflation driven by higher gas prices. The latest CPI index for gasoline was up 9.1% year over year in September 2026. Higher gas prices could hurt some retailers more than others, as consumers are compelled to dedicate more of their take-home pay to filling their tanks.

title: Walmart Stock Pops Following Deutsche Bank Upgrade
detail:
Walmart Stock Pops Following Deutsche Bank Upgrade
Aditya Raghunath
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 3:30 AM MST 3 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Walmart Stock Pops Following Deutsche Bank Upgrade ©@Bill Oxford from Getty Images Signature via Canva, @Alex Bascuas via Canva
Key Stats for Walmart Stock

Price change for Walmart stock in the last 6 months: -6%

$WMT Stock Price as of Oct. 15: $118

52-Week High: $135

$WMT Stock Price Target: $127

What Happened?

Walmart (WMT:NASDAQ) is getting a lift after Deutsche Bank upgraded it from Neutral to Buy on Thursday.

Analyst Krisztina Katai says higher inflation should help Walmart. Shoppers want value, and that plays to its strengths. She also thinks investors are starting to look past the weak U.S. comp number.

That number was soft as U.S. comp sales rose 2.6% in Q2, the slowest pace since Q4 of 2020. But Walmart says much of the drag comes from pharmacy.

New drug price rules cut about 1.25 percentage points from the comp and core categories have held in a steady 3% to 4% range.

The rest of the quarter looked strong:

Membership fee revenue rose 17%.

Sales rose 5% in constant currency.

Global e-commerce sales grew 23%.

Advertising grew 38%, and U.S. marketplace sales grew 52%.

WMT Stock Revenue, EBIT and Free Cash Flow Estimates in Billion USD (TIKR)

Those last three are higher-profit businesses, so they help margins.

Management also raised its full-year outlook. It now expects sales to grow 4% to 5% and operating income to grow 7% to 8.5%. EPS is guided to $2.80 to $2.87.

What the Market Is Telling Us About Walmart Stock

Investors seem to be betting that Walmart stock can win in a tough spending climate.

September inflation hit 3.7%, up from 3.4% in August. Grocery prices rose 1.8% but were roughly flat from the prior month.

Katai spoke with CFO John David Rainey. He said consumer trends were stable to improving compared with three months ago. He also said Walmart's price gaps versus rivals remain strong.

Walmart is backing that up with lower prices. It ran more than 11,000 rollbacks last quarter, up from 7,200 at the end of Q1.

Private-label sales are also growing as a share of the mix, up 1.3 percentage points from last year.

The company is pushing fashion brands like Scoop, Free Assembly and Scenario to attract higher-income shoppers.

WMT Stock Valuation Model (TIKR)

The price cuts will weigh on near-term profit, and Walmart expects Q3 operating income growth of just 2% to 4%.

It also sees more than $2 billion in extra fuel costs this year. Q2 profit growth of 17.4% also got a boost from tariff refunds, so the underlying number was lower.

For now, the market is looking past the soft comp. Walmart stock is being treated as a share-gainer in a tight consumer environment.

title: Kraft Heinz vs. Monster Beverage: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Kraft Heinz vs. Monster Beverage: Which Consumer Goods Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Jack Delaney, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 7:50 PM MST 6 min read
MNST
WMT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Should you invest in Kraft Heinz (NYSE:KHC) or Monster Beverage (NASDAQ:MNST)? One is better known for stability, while the other offers greater potential for stock price appreciation. Choosing between them depends on your specific financial goals.

Investors looking for stability often turn to the consumer defensive sector because of its consistent demand regardless of the economy. Kraft Heinz offers a wide array of household brands, while Monster dominates the high-margin energy drink space. This comparison explores which business model offers greater long-term value.

The case for Kraft Heinz

Kraft Heinz produces branded food products for home and restaurant use, making it a prominent name among consumer staples stocks. A significant portion of its success depends on large retail partners, including supermarkets and warehouse clubs. Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) is its most critical customer, accounting for approximately 21% of net sales in FY 2025. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In FY 2025, revenue reached $24.9 billion, which is a decrease of approximately 3.5% from the previous year. The company reported a net loss of close to $5.8 billion for the period. This result was primarily due to significant non-cash impairment charges, which occur when the value of assets like brands or goodwill drops below their recorded balance sheet value.

Kraft Heinz has total cash of $2.6 billion, with total debt of $19 billion, resulting in a 52.5% total debt-to-equity ratio. Its operating cash flow for the trailing 12-month period is $4.6 billion, and its leveraged free cash flow for the same period is $3.2 billion.

The case for Monster Beverage

Monster Beverage develops and distributes energy drinks under brands like Monster Energy and Reign. It relies heavily on a global distribution network, mainly through partnerships with Coca-Cola (NYSE:KO) bottlers. One partner, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (NASDAQ:CCEP), accounted for nearly 15% of net sales in FY 2025. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In FY 2025, revenue reached approximately $8.3 billion, indicating sales growth of 10.8%. Net income for the year was roughly $1.9 billion, a noticeable increase from the $1.5 billion reported in 2024. Revenue growth remained consistent as the company expanded its presence in international markets.

Monster is essentially debt free, with $3.4 billion in cash and $92.9 million worth of debt. Its debt-to-equity ratio sits at 0.9%. Operating cash flow for the trailing 12-month period is $2.2 billion, while leveraged free cash flow is $1.6 billion.
